title: What training does Japan's economic security clearance system require of cleared businesses?
description: Japan's security clearance law (in force May 16, 2025): education duties for cleared businesses, annual training, suitability assessment and penalties.
shortAnswer: Japan's Act on the Protection and Utilization of Critical Economic Security Information (Act No. 27 of 2024), in force since May 16, 2025, requires contracts with cleared businesses to cover employee education (Article 10(3)). The Cabinet Office guideline for businesses expects education before anyone first handles the information and at least once a year after that, delivered by the protection officer using materials submitted with the certification application.
keyTakeaways: Article 10(3) requires every contract between a government agency and a cleared business to set out matters on "education concerning the protection of" Critical Economic Security Information for employees.
The government's operational standards require a business seeking certification to have internal rules that specify the content and method of employee education, among 14 required items.

The Cabinet Office guideline for businesses (May 2, 2025) expects education at least once a year and before a person first handles the information; its template contract and template rules say the same.
Handling is limited to people found unlikely to leak the information in a suitability assessment within the past 10 years (Article 11(1)), covering seven investigation items (Article 12(2)).
A person handling the information who leaks it faces up to five years' imprisonment or a fine of up to JPY 5 million, or both, and Article 28 extends fines to the employing company.
regulator: Cabinet Office (Director-General for Economic Security), with the heads of the administrative organs that designate and provide Critical Economic Security Information
appliesTo: Businesses certified as conforming businesses (適合事業者) that receive Critical Economic Security Information under a contract with a government agency
Employees of those businesses who handle the information, after a favorable suitability assessment
The business's protection officer (保護責任者) and site business managers (業務管理者)
Officials of administrative organs that handle the information

sections.heading: What is Japan's economic security clearance system?

blocks.text: It is a statutory regime that lets the government share designated economic security information with vetted businesses and people. The [Cabinet Office page on the Act](https://www.cao.go.jp/keizai_anzen_hosho/hogokatsuyou/hogokatsuyou.html) records that the Act on the Protection and Utilization of Critical Economic Security Information (Act No. 27 of 2024) was enacted on May 10, 2024 and promulgated on May 17, 2024. The Cabinet Office's detailed overview gives May 16, 2025 as the date set by Cabinet Order for its entry into force.

Under Article 3(1), heads of administrative organs designate as Critical Economic Security Information non-public information about the protection of critical economic infrastructure whose leakage could harm national security. The overview gives examples such as detailed government response plans for cyberattacks on critical infrastructure and information on supply chain vulnerabilities for critical goods. Designations last up to five years at a time under Article 4, extendable as the Act allows.

Businesses enter the system when an agency wants them to use the information. Under Article 10(1), the agency may provide it to a conforming business, one that meets Cabinet Order criteria such as having the necessary facilities, under a contract. The scheme sits alongside Japan's earlier specially designated secrets regime, and Article 11(2) lets people cleared under that regime handle the new category for five years without a fresh assessment.

sections.heading: What does the Act require on education?

blocks.text: The Act makes employee education a mandatory contract term. According to the Cabinet Office's detailed overview, Article 10(3) requires contracts with conforming businesses to specify the range of employees designated to handle the information, the appointment of a person to manage protection, the facilities required, "matters relating to education concerning the protection of Critical Economic Security Information for employees", the duty to provide the information back to the agency on request, and other matters set by Cabinet Order. Article 10(4) requires the business to take the protective measures in the contract.

The government's [operational standards](https://www.cao.go.jp/keizai_anzen_hosho/hogokatsuyou/doc/kijun.pdf) make education a certification criterion. In Chapter 5, the head of the agency reviewing an application must check that the business has internal rules covering 14 items, including the nomination of a protection officer and site business managers and "the content and method of education on the protection of Critical Economic Security Information for employees". The application form requires an education implementation plan (timing, topics, place, audience and instructor) and a description of the education system, including the instructors' experience and their own training history.

Chapter 1 of the operational standards also addresses individuals directly. It says those who handle the information must recognize that they may be targeted by approaches seeking leaks and must keep their sense of norms high, for example "by attending the education on the protection of Critical Economic Security Information" carried out under Articles 11(1)(ii) and 16(1)(i) of the Enforcement Order.

sections.heading: How often must cleared businesses train, and what must training cover?

blocks.text: The Cabinet Office expects education at least once a year and before anyone first handles the information. The [guideline for conforming businesses](https://www.cao.go.jp/keizai_anzen_hosho/hogokatsuyou/doc/jigyousyagl.pdf), published on May 2, 2025, states that agencies consider whether a business's education lets staff accurately acquire the necessary knowledge and is delivered "continuously at an appropriate frequency". It continues that, using the business's own materials, people responsible for protection such as the protection officer must provide education to those handling the information "at least once a year", and that new handlers must receive the same education before they handle it.

The guideline insists that materials reflect the business's real internal practice, not just the government template. Education materials must be attached to the certification application, and any change to their substance must be reported to and reviewed by the agency before it takes effect. The template contract's Article 3 requires education for the protection officer, site business managers and expected handlers, before first handling and "at least once a year" for current handlers, while allowing extra sessions when needed.

The guideline's template education materials list minimum topics for annual security education: the laws and rules of the secrecy system; the meaning and importance of security education; penalties and disciplinary measures for leaks; the business's own security rules; and other topics including the need-to-know principle, faithful implementation of internal rules, and cyber infection prevention and incident handling procedures.

sections.heading: Who may handle the information, and what does the suitability assessment cover?

blocks.text: Only people who passed a suitability assessment in the past 10 years may handle the information, with limited exceptions such as ministers. Article 12(2) sets seven investigation items: relationships with activities that damage critical economic infrastructure (including family members' names, dates of birth, nationalities and addresses); criminal and disciplinary history; history of mishandling information; drug abuse; mental illness; moderation in drinking; and credit and other financial circumstances.

For employees of a conforming business, the business first selects candidates and prepares a list with their consent, and the agency then seeks consent again before investigating. The employee submits the questionnaire directly to the agency. Article 13 requires the result to be notified to the person, the Prime Minister and, for employees, the business. Article 16 bars the business from using the result for any purpose other than protecting the information, which matters for HR training on confidentiality.

sections.heading: What are the penalties and oversight mechanisms?

blocks.text: Leaks carry criminal penalties for individuals and fines for companies. Under Article 23(1), a person engaged in handling who leaks information learned in that work faces imprisonment of up to five years or a fine of up to JPY 5 million, or both, including after leaving the role; attempts and negligent leaks are also punishable. Article 24 applies the same maximum to acquiring the information by deception, violence, theft, intrusion or unauthorized access, and Article 27 covers acts abroad.

Article 28 is a dual liability provision: where an employee or agent commits an intentional leak or unlawful acquisition in connection with the company's business, the company is also fined. Article 19 requires the government to report annually to the Diet on designations, assessments and certifications, with experts' opinions; the Cabinet Office posted a report on June 26, 2026. As at November 2026, the Act, operational standards and guideline described here are in force.

sections.heading: How should a business prepare its clearance education program?

items: Appoint the protection officer and site business managers and confirm their own knowledge, since the application asks for instructors' experience and training history.
Draft internal rules covering the 14 items, with the education clause describing content, method, audience and frequency.
Write education materials from the template topics but describe the business's actual procedures, areas, devices and reporting lines.
Deliver education to each new handler before access and to every handler at least annually; add sessions after incidents or rule changes.
Submit material changes to the agency before using them, and keep version history.
Brief HR on the Article 16 restriction and on reporting changes in cleared employees' circumstances.

blocks.text: Companies in defense and critical supply chains can compare this with the [Defence Industry Security Program](/regulations/defence-industry-security-program-requirements) and [NISPOM security training](/regulations/nispom-security-training-requirements). Sector context is on the [government and defense](/industries/government-defence) page.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each contract term, internal rule item and guideline expectation as an obligation linked to the roles and assessment points that evidence it. When internal rules or education materials change, the items needing agency review and the people needing retraining can be traced from the changed clause.

faqs.q: Is the annual education requirement in the Act itself?
faqs.a: Not in those words. The Act requires education to be a contract term (Article 10(3)), the operational standards require internal rules on education content and method, and the Cabinet Office guideline and template contract set the at least once a year and before first handling expectations. In practice they become binding through the contract the business signs.

faqs.q: Does clearance under the specially designated secrets system carry over?
faqs.a: Partly. Article 11(2) allows a person found suitable under the Act on the Protection of Specially Designated Secrets to handle Critical Economic Security Information for five years without a new assessment. The business's own education duties under its contract still apply to that person.

faqs.q: Can a business create its own education materials?
faqs.a: It must. The business guideline says materials must be prepared by the business and explain its actual internal practice, using the government template only as a minimum. The materials are attached to the certification application, and substantive changes must be reviewed by the agency before they are used.

The guideline expects people responsible for protection, such as the protection officer or site business managers, to provide it. The certification application asks for the department responsible, each instructor's role and protection experience, and their record of attending security education, so instructors need their own documented training.

factCheck.claim: Act No. 27 of 2024 enacted 10 May 2024 and promulgated 17 May 2024; guidelines and Q&A posted 2 May 2025; protection rules posted 16 May 2025; report to the Diet posted 26 June 2026

Overview: in force on the date set by Cabinet Order (16 May 2025); Article 10(3) contract items include education on protection for employees; Article 11(1) handling limited to those assessed within 10 years; Article 11(2) five year carry-over for specially designated secrets clearance; Article 12(2) seven investigation items; Article 13 notification; Article 16 no other use; Article 19 annual Diet report; Article 4 five year designation period

Overview penalties: Article 23(1) up to 5 years imprisonment or JPY 5 million fine or both, including after leaving, attempts and negligence punishable; Article 24 unlawful acquisition same maximum; Article 27 acts abroad; Article 28 dual liability for corporations

Operational standards Chapter 5 Section 1, 2(2): certification review checks rules covering items including protection officer, business manager and (3) content and method of education for employees; application form section 3 requires education implementation plan and education system with instructors' experience and training record; rules must include all items (1) to (14)
Operational standards Chapter 1, 3: handlers should keep norms high by attending education on protection carried out under Enforcement Order Article 11(1)(ii) and Article 16(1)(i)

Business guideline Chapter 1 Section 2.2: education must enable accurate acquisition of knowledge and be continuous at appropriate frequency; materials prepared by the business reflecting internal practice and attached to the application; education at least once a year by the protection officer or similar to handlers; new handlers educated before handling

Business guideline: template rules Article 12 (annual education, before first handling, report changes); template contract Article 3 (education before handling, at least once a year, ad hoc allowed) and Article 4(2) agency review before changing rules or education materials; template education materials list minimum annual topics including laws and rules, importance, penalties and discipline, internal rules, need-to-know, cyber infection prevention
